# Welcome

> This space is where I share thoughts, tips, and notes about cybersecurity, development, and other tech stuff.

- [Welcome](https://blog.julez.cat/index.md): Welcome

## Articles

### DevSecOps

- [Commits signing](https://blog.julez.cat/articles/devsecops/commits-signing.md): Git allows anyone to set any name and email on a commit. This makes it trivial for an attacker to impersonate another contributor in the Git history.
- [What is DevSecOps ?](https://blog.julez.cat/articles/devsecops/devsecops-definition.md): TL;DR – DevSecOps integrates security from the first line of code through production operations, using collaboration and automation to make security everyone’s job and deliver software both fast and safe.

### Dorking

- [Google Dorking Guide](https://blog.julez.cat/articles/dorking/google-dorking.md): Google Dorking is legal as long as you're only passively viewing public search results.

### Homelab

- [Building a private-first homelab for apps and AI agents](https://blog.julez.cat/articles/homelab/homelab-architecture.md): TL;DR — My homelab is a small Debian server that runs my applications, deployment platform and AI development tooling. Public applications enter through
- [Public apps, private control plane: networking a Dokploy homelab](https://blog.julez.cat/articles/homelab/networking-and-exposure.md): Running an application at home is easy until it has to be reachable from the Internet.
- [Turning my homelab into an AI development environment](https://blog.julez.cat/articles/homelab/agentic-development.md): My homelab started as a place to deploy applications. It gradually became something more interesting: a development environment where AI agents can work on real repositories, run tools and ship changes through the same Git workflow I use manually.
